back: The downslope movement of rock, regolith and soil under gravity; water often helps by adding weight and reducing friction.
Heave (creep), flow (mudflow, debris flow), slide (translational, rotational) and fall (rock fall); classified by speed and water content.
The pressure of water between soil particles; when it rises it reduces friction and shear strength, making failure more likely.
Weak or weathered rock, dipping layers, steep slopes, heavy rainfall, earthquakes, undercutting and climate change.
Cutting into slopes for roads and buildings, loading, deforestation, leaking pipes, poor drainage, quarrying and mining.
Rock pinning and bolting, netting, grading and terracing, drainage, retaining walls, afforestation, planning, education and early warning.
Zoning land by slope, geology, vegetation and past events; monitoring with rain gauges, piezometers, extensometers, tiltmeters and satellites.
March 2019: days of heavy rain on steep slopes in the Eastern Highlands caused landslides and debris flows; hundreds of people died in Zimbabwe and roads and bridges were destroyed.
Score = Σ (factor score × weight); compare with class limits (low, moderate, high) to map the hazard.
